title: Constructor return types
answer: A constructor has no return type—not even `void`. Its name matches the class name, and a normal `new` expression produces the object reference after construction completes. If you write `void ClassName()`, that declaration is an ordinary method, not a constructor. When no constructor is declared, the compiler may provide a default no-argument constructor, which is why a class containing only such a void method can still be instantiated.
